pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Define and complete the **CAP Core v1 freeze boundary** before expanding the product mainly by adding more application/provider integrations.

This is intentionally different from PR #164:

- #164 asks how to broaden real-application physical coverage;
- this PR asks what must be true before the **CAP trust/control kernel can be considered stable**, so later Browser/Desktop/Procedure/Session/MCP/provider implementations can attach without rewriting core authority semantics.

Live research base:

`main@24ed938c587c9d3e2288c92bc156ccc476c955f3`

## Stage Research

Decision: **NARROW — finish the trust/core seams; do not build a universal plugin framework.**

### Stage goal

Reach a state where an implementation added inside an already accepted capability family normally changes:

```text
provider implementation
+ focused adapter/binding
+ conformance/security/physical evidence
```

and does **not** require changing:

```text
Control Plane authority
WorkingState semantics
operation/attempt/reconciliation identity
Verification Kernel
Finish Gate
public Chat schema
```

A genuinely new consequence class is explicitly outside that promise and may still require a new reviewed public/capability contract.

### Current core that is already strong

The repository already has genuinely provider-neutral foundations:

- `ObservationRef / ObservationSnapshot`;
- `ExpectedEffect`;
- `PASS | FAIL | UNKNOWN`;
- independent `FinishGateResult`;
- `WorkingState`;
- stable operation/attempt identity;
- typed mutating outcomes;
- reconciliation-before-retry;
- LoopGuard and budgets;
- provider-independent Delegation identity/result correlation;
- environmental content != authority.

These should be **KEEP**, not redesigned.

### Concrete coupling found during audit

1. **Control Plane package import has provider/application side effects.**

   `runtime/control_plane/__init__.py` currently contains Windows-native handle logic and patches the concrete `verified_workspace_artifact` procedure at import time. A caller importing the Control Plane package therefore crosses into Windows/file-procedure implementation details.

2. **Generic Delegation persistence reuses a procedure-private helper.**

   `delegation_state.py` imports local lock/path primitives from
   `_verified_workspace_artifact_support`. The mechanics are useful and accepted, but their ownership is incorrectly named/located for a generic lifecycle consumer.

3. **Browser and Files provider mechanics are embedded in semantic projection.**

   `semantic-projection.mjs` resolves/spawns the filesystem MCP server and Playwright MCP directly. The public semantic contract and provider implementation are therefore in the same runtime module.

4. **Registered procedures are intentionally hard-admitted in both Node and Python.**

   This is not automatically a defect. `procedure_run` is a reviewed bounded semantic surface, not a plugin dispatcher. Core v1 must not “fix” this by loading arbitrary procedure manifests or raw MCP catalogs.

### Architecture lineage

| Role | Prior owner | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| General planner | ordinary ChatGPT | **KEEP** |
| Authority / grants / WorkingState | project Control Plane | **KEEP** |
| Verification | project Verification Kernel | **KEEP** |
| Task completion | project Finish Gate | **KEEP** |
| Browser execution | Playwright behind Browser capability | **REFINE** — provider mechanics move behind a Browser-specific seam; Playwright stays default |
| Files backend | reviewed filesystem semantic adapter | **REFINE** — separate provider implementation from semantic contract |
| Optional MCP lifecycle | 1MCP / qualified replacement | **KEEP** — discovery/lifecycle only, never trust/authorization |
| Delegation lifecycle | project-owned Delegation state | **KEEP / REUSE_MORE** — move shared local-state primitives to correctly owned core utility |
| Full CapabilityRegistry/EventBus | ADR-037 future | **DEFER** — not needed to freeze Core v1 |
| Universal provider/meta-tool | none | **REJECT** |

### External mechanism evidence

The selected direction follows several mature patterns without copying any one system wholesale.

**Kubernetes CRI**

Kubernetes uses a narrow runtime interface so kubelet can use different container runtimes without deep per-runtime integration or recompilation. Common lifecycle/control semantics remain in kubelet rather than being reimplemented by every runtime.

- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/cri/
- https://kubernetes.io/blog/2016/12/container-runtime-interface-cri-in-kubernetes/

Lesson for CAP: define narrow interfaces **per capability role**, while keeping retries/authority/verification in the core.

**VS Code Extension Host**

VS Code runs extensions in dedicated extension-host runtimes and activates them according to declared capabilities/location rather than merging extension code into the UI/core process.

- https://code.visualstudio.com/api/advanced-topics/extension-host

Lesson for CAP: extension/provider runtime location/lifecycle is separate from semantic authority.

**Vault / Nomad plugins**

Vault verifies registered plugin artifacts before execution and communicates with external plugin processes over authenticated RPC; Nomad defines distinct plugin types/interfaces rather than one arbitrary “do anything” call.

- https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/plugins/plugin-architecture
- https://developer.hashicorp.com/nomad/plugins/author

Lesson for CAP: explicit provider identity/provenance and role-specific interfaces are stronger than a universal generic dispatcher.

**MCP 2026-07-28**

Current MCP separates protocol core, transports, authorization and formal extensions; the protocol is an integration substrate, not an application-specific authority model.

- https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/
- https://go.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/

Lesson for CAP: reuse MCP for transport/discovery where useful, but keep CAP authorization/effect/completion semantics above it.

### Alternatives

#### A. One universal Provider API / raw generic dispatcher — REJECT

Example shape:

`invoke(provider, operation, arbitrary_json)`

This would recreate the already rejected generic meta-tool problem, make consequence classes opaque and move security burden into runtime conventions.

#### B. Keep integrating each backend directly into semantic/core modules — REJECT

This preserves current behavior but guarantees increasing coupling and makes “Core v1 freeze” meaningless.

#### C. Stable trust core + capability-specific provider seams — SELECT

```text
ChatGPT
 -> stable semantic capability
 -> CAP authority / state / verification
 -> capability-specific adapter seam
 -> provider
```

The provider may be Playwright today and BrowserSkill later; the core consequence contract does not change merely because execution mechanics change.

#### D. Implement ADR-037 CapabilityRegistry/EventBus now — DEFER

It may become useful once multiple live providers need runtime discovery/routing/events. Today it adds infrastructure without solving the concrete coupling already found.

### Architecture primitives introduced in the first implementation slice

Only two refactoring primitives are admitted:

1. **provider-neutral local state utility ownership**
   - move accepted lock/path persistence helpers out of a procedure-private module so Delegation and procedures reuse them without inverted dependency;

2. **pure Core API boundary**
   - create/import a provider-neutral core surface that has no Windows/browser/application side effects.

No dynamic plugin loader, generic provider registry, EventBus, scheduler, raw tool dispatcher or new public tool is introduced.

A later Browser/Files provider extraction may proceed only after the first slice proves the purity boundary and its tests; if that extraction introduces dynamic routing/authority or new persistence, Stage Research re-enters.

### Failure / authority matrix

| Boundary | Failure | Required behavior |
|---|---|---|
| import core contracts | provider runtime unavailable / non-Windows host | core import still succeeds; no provider launch/patch side effects |
| provider binding | unknown/unreviewed provider | unavailable/ABSTAIN; never auto-authorize |
| provider receipt | provider says “success” | evidence only; no direct project PASS/DONE |
| provider identity changes | stale receipt/runtime | provenance mismatch -> UNKNOWN/ABSTAIN |
| optional MCP disappears | backend unavailable | affected capability unavailable; core and unrelated capabilities remain healthy |
| provider-specific state | session/HWND/tool id leaks upward | may be referenced as provenance/native observation, never redefine logical operation/grant identity |
| new consequence class appears | adapter tries to hide it under existing semantics | stop; separate public/security Stage Research required |
| shared persistence helper fails | ambiguous local state | preserve existing fail-closed/reconciliation behavior; no semantic weakening from refactor |

### Failure shields

The first implementation slice must add tests proving:

- provider-neutral core import does not import Windows/browser/application implementation modules;
- importing the core performs no filesystem/browser/Win32 monkey-patching;
- generic Delegation state no longer depends on a workspace-artifact-private helper module;
- existing WorkingState/verification/delegation serialized behavior remains byte/semantics compatible where required;
- current six-tool inventory is unchanged;
- no new generic dispatch surface exists.

### Acceptance ladder

**L1**

- import/dependency-boundary tests;
- existing verification/WorkingState/Delegation tests;
- no semantic/public inventory change.

**L2**

- existing procedure and semantic projection integration regressions;
- Windows-specific procedure behavior remains loaded only by its owning runtime path;
- existing hosted CI/security gates.

**L3**

No new physical acceptance is required for a pure internal extraction that provably does not change physical behavior. Any later provider-binding implementation that changes real Browser/Windows execution does require the capability's normal physical gate.

## Scope

This PR starts with the architecture freeze definition already added to `project-context/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

The next implementation commits may only:

1. establish a pure provider-neutral Control Plane core import surface;
2. move already-accepted local-state primitives to neutral ownership without semantic change;
3. add structural/adversarial tests for those boundaries.

Browser/File provider extraction comes after this first slice and only if it can preserve the selected architecture without introducing an uncovered dynamic routing/authority primitive.

PR #159 remains separate and still requires its own exact-head fresh review + target-Windows reviewer qualification.
PR #164 remains a separate broad-app qualification research track and does not define Core v1.


## Implementation status / sequencing

First Core-v1 extraction slice is now implemented on this Draft branch:

- generic Delegation and independent-review state use neutral `runtime/control_plane/local_state.py` rather than workspace-procedure-private helpers;
- plain `import runtime.control_plane` exposes provider-neutral authority/state/verification contracts without importing Windows/file/provider implementations;
- the existing Stage 26.3C workspace hardening is preserved behind an explicit two-phase procedure-owned bootstrap so pre-import delivery-proof hooks still bind before by-value helper imports;
- production manager and standalone semantic installed-layout manifests both carry the new runtime dependencies;
- focused boundary tests cover import purity, lazy compatibility export, shared local-state ownership and installed-manifest completeness.

A first refactor attempt exposed two concrete failure classes and both were closed by class:

1. late procedure hardening missed a support helper imported by value; the fix is explicit pre-import + post-import phases, with Stage 26.3A remaining the behavioral guard;
2. a new runtime dependency was present in the production manager bundle but absent from the standalone semantic acceptance copy; both manifests are now guarded together.

### Merge sequencing lock

This PR **must remain Draft and must not merge before PR #159 completes its exact-base fresh review and target-Windows physical reviewer gate**.

PR #159 is still based on `main@24ed938c587c9d3e2288c92bc156ccc476c955f3`. Merging this Core-v1 branch first would change that base and invalidate #159's exact-base acceptance identity. After #159 is accepted/merged, this branch must be rebased/refreshed against the new main and its applicable bootstrap/research/review gates rerun before merge.

The broad real-application matrix in #164 likewise remains a later independent track; it does not authorize widening this Core-v1 refactor.
